gap.title: An AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 24 gates computes the edge function of the listed graph on 14 vertices with 19 edges
gap.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 24 ∧ (∀ x : Fin 14 → Bool, (C.eval (List.ofFn x) = true ↔ ∃ u v : Fin 14, (u.val, v.val) ∈ ([(0, 8), (0, 10), (1, 7), (1, 9), (1, 13), (2, 8), (2, 13), (3, 7), (3, 11), (3, 12), (4, 10), (4, 11), (4, 13), (5, 9), (5, 10), (5, 12), (6, 8), (6, 9), (6, 11)] : List (ℕ × ℕ)) ∧ x u = true ∧ x v = true))
gap.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
gap.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. Proved by exhibiting ONE circuit with at most the stated number of gates of fan-in at most two that computes the edge function (true exactly when both ends of some edge are true) on every input; checked by evaluation. The best circuit known to us has one gate more (computed, not checked). Size: minutes if such a circuit exists. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
